hardcoded_assumptions.why_dangerous: USER ID 1 IS HARDCODED TO ALWAYS BE ACTIVE on every save. If admin user happens to be id=1 (typical), they CANNOT BE DISABLED — any update reactivates them. Bypass of disablement. In V2 multi-tenant SaaS this is a tenant-wide super-admin backdoor.
hardcoded_assumptions.exploit: 1. Admin gets compromised, owner disables user_id=1. 2. ANY subsequent update on that user (timezone change, name change, password reset triggered) resets status=ACTIVE. 3. Compromised credentials remain usable.

hardcoded_assumptions.why_dangerous: Language id=1 is hardcoded as undeletable. If a future migration changes seed order, deletes id=1, or DemoSeed reseeds with different IDs, language tooling breaks silently.

Customer loyalty token = SHA256(user_id | unix_timestamp | APP_KEY) truncated to 32 hex chars (128 bits). NO HMAC despite LOYALTY_QR_SECRET being declared elsewhere in the codebase for QR signing. Timestamp is SECOND-RESOLUTION → if attacker observes account creation time (visible in many UIs) AND knows user_id (sequential), they can brute-force the 1-second window. SHA256(known)+128 bit truncation = NOT collision-safe over 6-year horizon if collision-finding becomes cheaper.
Coupon discount_type magic number 1 hardcoded instead of named enum. If enum values change, silent miscalculation.

HOWEVER: 2 confessed P0 hardcoded assumptions (User.php id===1 + LoyaltyController predictable token) are NOT IN ANY PROPOSAL DOC and NOT in the owner-gate queue. The H.5 'critical bug healed' pattern (fixture masked) recurs in 30+ regression tests unaddressed. Phase I.6 corrected BRAIN §9 from stale 8 to stale 13 (actual 21) — BRAIN drift cascades.
